items.title: Appeals court upholds Yoon's election law conviction, putting PPP funds at risk
items.title_zh: 上诉法院维持Yoon的选举法定罪，使PPP资金面临风险
items.summary: An appellate court on Wednesday upheld the conviction of former President Yoon Suk Yeol for making false statements during his 2022 presidential campaign, a ruling that, if finalized, would require the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) to repay 39.7 billion won ($30 million) in campaign reimbursements. The Seoul High Court upheld a lower court’s sentence of 18 months in prison, suspended for three years, over statements Yoon made before his election in March 2022. The decision leaves the PPP facing a substantial financial liability, although the repayment obligation depends on the conviction becoming final at the Supreme Court. Under the election law, the government fully reimburses campaign expenses for political parties whose presidential candidates receive at least 15 percent of the vote. But the funds must be returned if a candidate receives a final prison sentence or a fine of at least 1 million won for election law violations. Such a penalty also invalidates the candidate’s election.

A government task force comprising officials from the education and health ministries first selected North Gyeongsang and South Jeolla provinces as sites for the new medical schools after finding they suffer from poor access to medical services and need a foundation for training and retaining physicians. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday it will work with city police authorities to review race schedules, routes, traffic diversions and safety management plans for 2027. items.title: Sejong University professor explores conditions for scientific development on exoplanets
items.title_zh: 世宗大学教授探索系外行星科学发展的条件
items.summary: A Sejong University professor has published a study in an international astronomy journal exploring how the astronomical environments of exoplanets could influence the scientific development of potential intelligent life. The study by Zee Woong-bae, a professor at the university’s School of Liberal Studies, was published last month in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society under the title “Alien Skies: Visibility of Planetary Retrograde Motion from Rocky Habitable-Zone Worlds.” The university said the study goes beyond existing research into conditions that could support extraterrestrial life, focusing instead on astronomical environments that could enable intelligent life on exoplanets to develop science and technology. Until now, the search for extraterrestrial life has concentrated on environmental conditions that could support life, such as planetary temperatures and the possibility of liquid water. The Republic of Korea Navy Task Fleet Command is taking part in the drills, which kicked off Sunday for a six-day run, involving nearly a dozen warships and other aircraft, according to the Navy. Deployed assets include the Navy's 8,200-ton Jeongjo the Great destroyer, the ROKS Yulgok Yi I destroyer, auxiliary ships, frigates, and patrol aircraft. During the drills, the Navy will train under simulated attack scenarios involving air defense combat, antisubmarine warfare and antisurface warfare, and conduct drills to detect and track ballistic missile launches. The command also took part in maritime drills in southern waters off Jeju Island early Wednesday, involving the Marado amphibious assault ship and other amphibious ships deployed as part of a joint training mission the previous day. In an interview with The Korea Times in September, IES Global President and CEO Gregory Hess emphasized that Korea is rapidly gaining ground as a study abroad destination for American students, attracting growing interest not only for its cultural appeal but also for its technological prowess and world-class universities. "Korea is one of the hot countries," he said. "Students are attracted not only to its culture, its entrepreneurial culture, the prominence of its products, but also the great universities that are here." items.title: Ruling party proposes gov't delay planned taxation of cryptocurrency
items.title_zh: 执政党建议政府不要推迟对加密货币征税的计划
items.summary: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) on Wednesday formally proposed that the government postpone the implementation of taxation on cryptocurrencies, set to take effect next year. The party's supreme council decided to make such a proposal in a meeting, considering the need to give businesses and investors time to adjust to the new taxation scheme, according to DPK leader Kim Min-seok. "We agreed that it would be better to first enact the Digital Asset Basic Act to build an overall framework and allow time for companies and investors to adapt after a comprehensive review of taxation principles, domestic industry conditions and fairness among users," Rep. Kim said. Korea first introduced a taxation scheme on cryptocurrencies in 2020, but its implementation has been repeatedly postponed, with the taxation now set to take effect Jan. 1. If the latest proposal is accepted, it would mark the fourth delay. Under the scheme, annual cryptocurrency gains exceeding 2.5 million won ($1,880) will be subject to a 22 percent tax, including the local income tax.

The NEC is also suspected of revising its internal guidelines to require all local election commissions to purchase ink and other supplies from the chosen company. A district court sentenced Yoon to an 18-month prison term, suspended for three years, in July after finding him guilty of the charges. items.title: Culture Minister meets Algerian president; visits Saudi pavilion at Algiers Book Fair
items.title_zh: 文化部长会见阿尔及利亚总统；参观阿尔及尔书展沙特馆
items.summary: ALGIERS — Algeria’s President Abdelmadjid Tebboune met with Saudi Minister of Culture Prince Badr bin Abdullah at the presidential palace in Algiers on Tuesday. The meeting took place during the minister’s visit to the 2026 Algiers International Book Fair in which Saudi Arabia is the guest of honor.Prince Badr conveyed to Tebboune the greetings of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman. He also conveyed their wishes for the president’s continued health and happiness and for Algeria and its people’s continued progress and prosperity.The minister congratulated the Algerian president for holding the 2026 Algiers International Book Fair. The meeting reaffirmed the deep-rooted relations between the two countries and the importance of cultural cooperation. It also emphasized the importance of coordinating positions on cultural matters within international and regional organizations to serve their mutual interests.Saudi Assistant Minister of Culture Rakan Al-Touq, Saudi Ambassador to Algeria Dr. Abdullah Al-Busairi, and Assistant Deputy Minister for International Cultural Relations Dr. Fahd Al-Humaidani also attended the meeting. **media[2789450]** Minister of Culture and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Literature, Publishing and Translation Commission Prince Badr bin Abdullah visited the Saudi pavilion at the 2026 Algiers International Book Fair, in the presence of Algerian Minister of Culture and Arts Dr. Malika Bendouda.Saudi Arabia’s participation in the fair, which runs through November 7, introduces visitors of various nationalities to Saudi culture, its rich historical heritage, and its literary output. Participating entities include the Literature, Publishing and Translation Commission; the Culinary Arts Commission; King Salman Global Academy for Arabic Language; Prince Mohammed bin Salman Global Center for Arabic Calligraphy (Dar Alqalam); King Abdulaziz Public Library; King Fahd National Library; the Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Call and Guidance; King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex in Madinah; the Saudi Cultural Mission in Algeria; King Abdulaziz Complex for Endowment Libraries; and the Arab Observatory of Translation.Saudi Arabia’s participation reflects its commitment to culture as a key pillar of Saudi Vision 2030, which has strengthened the sector’s role in development and broadened opportunities for creativity, knowledge production, and cultural exchange worldwide.The participation also highlights the role of books in connecting peoples, deepening historical and cultural ties, and promoting dialogue and the exchange of literary and intellectual experiences. These efforts enrich the Arab cultural landscape and reinforce Arabic as a vehicle for knowledge and a pillar of shared identity.

items.title: Saudi Arabia’s FDI inflows surge 33.5% to SR159 billion in 2025

items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia recorded a remarkable increase of 33.5 percent in foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in 2025 compared with 2024, reaching approximately SR159 billion. The growth reflects the Kingdom’s increasing appeal to foreign investors and its continued progress toward achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030.Alongside this growth, the stock of FDI in Saudi Arabia increased by 8.3 percent to reach SR1,059 billion by the end of 2025, surpassing the SR1 trillion mark and reflecting the expansion of the foreign investment base in the Saudi economy. The scale of this progress becomes more evident when compared with 2017 levels. FDI inflows increased more than fivefold over the period, while the stock of FDI doubled. The compound annual growth rate stood at 24 percent for inflows and 10 percent for the FDI stock, underscoring the scale of the Kingdom’s economic transformation in recent years.FDI inflows are among the indicators used to measure the performance of the National Transformation Program (NTP) against its strategic objective of attracting foreign and domestic investment. Initiatives under the program, led by the Ministry of Investment in coordination with relevant entities, are helping improve the investment environment, enhance its competitiveness, and attract high-quality investment to Saudi Arabia.These results reflect the impact of the economic transformations and regulatory and structural reforms introduced since the launch of Saudi Vision 2030. The reforms have helped strengthen Saudi Arabia’s position as an attractive investment destination and reinforce international investors’ confidence in the opportunities and growth prospects of the Saudi economy.The NTP, one of the programs supporting the achievement of Saudi Vision 2030, continues to contribute to achieving 34 strategic objectives, representing approximately 35 percent of the Vision’s overall objectives. It encompasses more than 310 initiatives led by seven ministries and involving over 50 implementing entities. Progress toward its targets is measured through 78 domestic and international indicators.

items.title: Saudi, Romanian defense ministers discuss over phone enhancing military cooperation
items.title_zh: 沙特，罗马尼亚国防部长通过电话讨论加强军事合作
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman held a phone call on Tuesday with Romanian Minister of National Defense Stefan Radu Oprea.During the call, Prince Khalid congratulated the Romanian minister on his appointment as the minister of national defense. The ministers reviewed the existing military and defense cooperation between the two friendly countries and ways to strengthen and further develop it. They also discussed the latest regional and international developments.

items.title: Saudi Arabia vows firm response to any threat to national security, public safety
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯誓言坚决应对任何对国家安全和公共安全的威胁
items.summary: RIYADH — The Council of Ministers reaffirmed Saudi Arabia’s unwavering resolve to safeguard its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity, declaring that any threat or aggression against its national security or the safety of its citizens and residents would be met with a firm and resolute response. Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman chaired the Cabinet session in Riyadh on Tuesday. The Cabinet reviewed the latest regional and international developments, underscoring the Kingdom’s continued diplomatic engagement, in close coordination with friendly nations, to reinforce regional security, preserve stability, and advance the causes of development, prosperity and lasting peace for the peoples of the region. At the outset of the session, the Crown Prince briefed the Cabinet on the contents of the two messages addressed to Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and the Crown Prince from King of Malaysia Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar, as well as the message the Crown Prince sent to Chinese President Xi Jinping. He also briefed the Cabinet on his phone calls with Korean President Lee Jae Myung, President of Romania Nicușor Dan, and Prime Minister of Spain Pedro Sánchez, alongside the outcomes of his reception of Jordanian Crown Prince Al Hussein bin Abdullah. In a statement to the Saudi Press Agency following the session, Minister of Media Salman Al-Dossary said that the Cabinet reviewed the outcomes of Saudi Arabia's participation in meetings held under the auspices of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) and the G20. This was part of the Kingdom’s efforts to support multilateral action aimed at strengthening mechanisms for joint cooperation across various fields, serving mutual interests and benefits, and contributing to effective and sustainable solutions to current global challenges, particularly those related to maritime navigation security, energy, food security, global trade, and supply chains. The Cabinet reaffirmed the Kingdom's rejection of all violations that threaten the security and safety of maritime navigation and global energy supplies. It stressed the importance of urgent action by the international community to ensure maritime security, safeguard the flow of international trade, and enforce international law in this regard. The Cabinet affirmed that, despite the region's challenges, the Kingdom has continued to reliably supply energy to global markets, supported by long-term investments in infrastructure, storage facilities, and supply chains, as well as an ecosystem capable of responding to changing circumstances with the highest levels of technical and operational capability. These efforts have contributed to strengthening global energy security and the resilience of supply networks. The Cabinet authorized the chairman of the board of directors of the Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Commission or his deputy to discuss and sign two draft memoranda of understanding with the National Nuclear Regulator of South Africa and the National Nuclear Safety Authority of Brazil on the exchange of information in nuclear and radiological regulation. The Council authorized the chairman of the board of directors of the King Abdulaziz Foundation for Research and Archives (Darah) or his deputy to discuss and sign a draft cooperation agreement with the Bibliotheca Alexandrina of Egypt, and authorized the minister of human resources and social development or his deputy to discuss and sign a draft MoU between the Saudi and Syrian governments for cooperation in labor market development and skills building. The Cabinet approved a MoU for cooperation in water resources between the Saudi and Indian governments and another MoU between the Saudi Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Interior of Pakistan on developing scientific, training, and research cooperation. It approved a MoU for cooperation in radio and television broadcasting between the Saudi Broadcasting Authority and the Moroccan Public Broadcasting Company (SNRT). The Cabinet approved the National Space Policy. It endorsed the financial oversight rules for endowment accounts overseen or managed by a government entity. The Cabinet decided to transfer a number of the responsibilities and tasks of the Conventions and Exhibitions General Authority to the National Events Center and the Saudi Investment Promotion Authority.

items.title: ‘Absher Travel for Visitors’ users can access services through 992
items.title_zh: “Absher Travel for Visitors”用户可以通过992访问服务
items.summary: RIYADH — The General Directorate of Passports is receiving inquiries and providing support through its unified contact number, 992, for the nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states and other visitors using the ‘Absher Travel for Visitors’ service to enter Saudi Arabia through any land border crossing. The directorate said the initiative is part of the Ministry of Interior’s efforts to improve electronic services, enhance visitors’ experience, and facilitate entry procedures at land border crossings.

items.title: Saudi Arabia posts SR84 billion budget deficit in 3Q 2026
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯公布2026年第三季度预算赤字为840亿里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia registered a budget deficit of SR84 billion during the third quarter of 2026, according to the Ministry of Finance's quarterly budget performance report released on Tuesday. Total revenues reached SR 259.11 billion during the third quarter while expenditures stood at SR343.42 billion. The report revealed a 23 percent decline in oil revenues reaching SR116.5 billion, while non-oil revenues rose by 20 percent to SR142.6 billion during the third quarter of this year. For the first nine months of the year, total revenues stood at SR858.87 billion, compared with expenditures of SR1,103.17 billion, resulting in a cumulative budget deficit of SR244.31 billion. Oil revenues during the first nine months amounted to SR446.3 billion, while non-oil revenues totaled SR412.5 billion. Meanwhile, the state’s general reserve balance stood at SR399.5 billion at the end of the third quarter of 2026.

items.title: Border Guard rescues citizen after boat breaks down at sea
items.title_zh: 海上船只抛锚后边防队营救市民
items.summary: JEDDAH — Search and rescue teams from the Border Guard in Jeddah, in the Makkah region, rescued a Saudi citizen after his boat suffered a breakdown at sea and provided him with the necessary assistance.The General Directorate of the Border Guard urged beachgoers and sea users to strictly adhere to maritime safety guidelines and instructions, ensure that their vessels are seaworthy before setting sail, and wear life jackets. It also advised them to contact 911 in Makkah, Madinah, and the Eastern Province, and 994 in the rest of the Kingdom, to seek assistance in emergencies.

items.title: Houthi-fired UAV intercepted over Makkah region
items.title_zh: 胡塞武装发射的无人机在麦加地区上空被拦截
items.summary: RIYADH — Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen, announced on Tuesday the interception and destruction of a UAV in the Makkah region. This comes a day after the interception and destruction of a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militias towards the southern region, and two drones in the Riyadh region.

items.title: Saudi, US defense ministers discuss Houthi attacks, regional de-escalation in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特、美国国防部长在电话中讨论胡塞武装袭击、地区降级
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman held a phone call with US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Tuesday. During the call, they reviewed prospects for strategic defense cooperation between the two countries. They discussed regional and international developments, particularly efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region and the terrorist Houthi militia's continued attacks on Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Saudi Arabia recalls 1,262 RAM vehicles over trailer brake failure risk
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯召回超过拖车制动故障风险的1,262辆RAM车辆
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Commerce has recalled 1,262 RAM vehicles over a defect in the trailer control module that could cause the trailer’s brakes and lights to malfunction, increasing the risk of an accident. The recall covers RAM 1500, RAM 2500 and RAM 5500 vehicles from model years 2025 to 2026. According to the ministry, a defect in the trailer control module could cause the trailer’s turn signals and brake lights to malfunction and its braking system to become inoperative while being towed. Owners of affected vehicles are advised to check whether their Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) is included in the recall through Recalls.sa. The ministry urged affected owners to contact Petromin Stellantis at 8003030040 to arrange the necessary repairs free of charge.
